MANILA, Philippines – A former stockbroker, board director, and longtime government official will now take charge of the Philippines’ first sovereign wealth fund.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has appointed Ma. Angela “Angel” Ignacio as the next president and chief executive officer of the Maharlika Investment Corporation (MIC).

Ignacio succeeds Rafael “Joel” Consing Jr., whose three-year term ended on Monday, November 23. The appointment hardly comes as a surprise, with Ignacio’s name having made the rounds for months as Consing’s likely successor.

Prior to joining Maharlika, Ignacio headed the Department of Finance’s (DOF) Government Corporations and Investments Group, working closely with Finance Secretary Frederick Go, who also chairs MIC’s board.

All three previously worked at the now-defunct Office of the Special Assistant to the President for Investment and Economic Affairs, which Go headed before moving to the DOF. Ignacio served as an undersecretary, while Consing was its executive director before taking the top job at Maharlika.

Ignacio’s time in government spans several administrations. From 2011 to 2016, she served as a commissioner of the Governance Commission for Government-Owned or -Controlled Corporations (GOCC) under the Aquino administration. She also worked as a consultant for the World Bank and Asian Development Bank.
In the boardroom, Ignacio served as an independent director of Ayala Land and sat on the board of the state-owned United Coconut Planters Bank.

blocks.caption: The Maharlika fund that Joel Consing leaves behind

blocks.text: Ignacio said the President’s directive was to “make sure that Maharlika does what it was intended to do under the law.”

Recall that the sovereign wealth fund’s creation in 2023 drew a firestorm of criticism from economists and governance experts, who questioned its purpose in a country with little fiscal space or windfall revenues, its vulnerability to political meddling, and the wisdom of sourcing its start-up capital from state-owned banks.
Over the next 18 months, Ignacio intends to deploy more capital into power, energy, and infrastructure. She is also looking at opportunities in artificial intelligence, food security, and tourism.

Ignacio inherits a fund that has already assembled a team of around 60 professionals and established its investment policies and risk management procedures, but has been slow to put its capital to work. As of end-September, Maharlika had deployed only P24.7 billion and still held P53.67 billion in cash and cash equivalents.

Maharlika’s largest deployment under Consing was a P15-billion working capital loan to Petron Corporation, while its much-touted P19.7-billion deal that would have secured board seats in the country’s power grid operator was shelved. Only three days before Consing’s departure did Maharlika announce another strategic investment of up to P900 million in Tubig Pilipinas. – Rappler.com
